CETEARYL ALCOHOL (rank 2) — long-chain fatty alcohol in the top three: S2 satisfied
GLYCINE SOJA OIL (3), BUTYROSPERMUM PARKII BUTTER (5), COCOS NUCIFERA OIL (7) — three distinct non-fatty-alcohol lipids above the tail, none at tail_index − 1: S3 satisfied
PARFUM (rank 10) — tail marker, plausible under §3.1.1 (R2)
conditioningLevel.derivation: Recompute with every tail_index − 1 species removed (R3). S1 = NOT satisfied: BEHENTRIMONIUM METHOSULFATE @9 is excluded, leaving CETRIMONIUM CHLORIDE @6 as the only distinct cationic. S2 = satisfied. S3 = satisfied (three lipids, all ranked above tail_index − 1). Two signals fire, but S1 is not one of them.
thresholdReasoning: Clears `moderate`: §9.1 is explicit that S2 + S3 without S1 is `moderate`, because both of those signals read the fatty/emollient load, which is the axis §9.2 owns. Saying it twice would be the shared-mechanism double count §6 rule 1 forbids — and this product is the clearest cohort instance of that, since its richness is already said in `weight_potential: high`.
`high` does not apply: S1 is mandatory under R3 and fails on the tail-edge exclusion.
`low` does not apply: S2 and S3 both hold.

Material counter-signals checked and NOT fired: resolved, plausible marker; no §2.4.1 tier-2 conflict; no fired signal resting on a family-10 species (GLYCERYL STEARATE SE @14 is in the tail and was never counted).
counterSignals: The value hinges entirely on one rank: BEHENTRIMONIUM METHOSULFATE at 9 against PARFUM at 10. Its near-twin #10 has the same two cationics at @8 and @10 against a marker at 12, and therefore keeps `high`. §9.1 flags the width of the boundary band (one rank vs two) as the open calibration question; this pair is the cohort's sharpest test of it. See AP-03-TWINS and AP-03-TAILEDGE.
Long ingredient list and the rheology-only GLYCERYL STEARATE SE @14 and HYDROXYPROPYL GUAR HYDROXYPROPYLTRIMONIUM CHLORIDE @13 — §9.1 NON-material counter-signals: recorded, never capping.
Two hydrolyzed proteins (@15, @17) sit in the tail behind an 'SOS Protein' pack — a sub-1 % hero tail, recorded in `hinweise` and credited nowhere.
limitations: A three-step concentration scale is at the edge of INCI support; no published dataset maps INCI patterns to validated low/medium/high thresholds (§9.1 honest limitation).
Rank is used qualitatively only. EU Art. 19 hides the 1 % boundary; no percentage, ratio, dose or deposited amount is inferable.

primaryFocus.rationale: Every special-purpose route fails its own test, the D5 moisture guard fails on cluster size, and neither the shine nor the smoothing threshold is reachable without a silicone, polymer, or film former above the tail. What remains is a rich, capable, conventional mask whose distinguishing feature — richness — is the category baseline. §9.5.2 step 8 is the honest answer.

primaryFocus.derivation: Step 1 baseline exclusion applied. Step 2: the four lipids, two cationics and fatty alcohol are ONE M1 observation, not four focus candidates (§6 rule 1). Step 3: `repair` blocked (no R5 above tail, no bond); `curl_support` rejected (see threshold reasoning); `color_care` blocked; `lightness` blocked (weight is `high`). Step 4 `moisture` blocked at cluster size. Step 5 `shine` blocked (§9.5.4 criterion 1 — no alignment-oriented route above the tail, and an R4b heavy lipid IS above the tail). Step 6 `smoothing` rejected. Step 7 `detangling` rejected. Step 8 → `general`.
thresholdReasoning: Clears `general`: §9.5.2 step 8 — a capable conventional mask where no differentiator clears threshold and the formula evidence is nonspecific.

`curl_support` is the closest competitor and is REFUSED on principle. Its test is 'high slip PLUS compatible weight/body architecture', with curl positioning as corroboration only. Both legs are literally satisfiable here — but they are satisfied by nothing except the category baseline (a two-cationic cetearyl base plus lipids), which is exactly what §9.5.2 step 1 forbids from creating a focus. The only thing distinguishing this product from #01 HASK, whose architecture is comparably rich and which gets `general`, is the curl claim — and step 9 states positioning may corroborate but never create. Awarding `curl_support` here would be claim-creation wearing a formula test. See AP-03-CURLBAR.
`moisture` does not apply: the D5 guard needs ≥3 distinct humectants above the tail with ≥2 non-glycerin. Glycerin @4 and Betaine @8 give two, and Panthenol @11 falls one rank below the marker.

`smoothing` does not apply: step 6 requires the architecture to extend materially beyond the ordinary mask base via a distinct silicone, substantive polymer, or substantial lipid/emollient route. The lipid route qualifies for that conjunct, but dry surface control is not this formula's clearest practical differentiator — there is no silicone, no polymer and no film former above the tail, and the credited route is softening rather than surface control.
`detangling` does not apply: slip is category baseline (§9.5.2 step 7's stated expectation), and nothing here makes it distinctive relative to competing routes.

This product and #10 receive an identical nine-field profile despite occupying different archetype slots (3 'protein bomb' vs 9 'curl mask') — see AP-03-TWINS.

adjudicationPoints.title: R3's tail-edge exclusion moves this product's conditioning_level, which the ruling ledger did not predict — ESCALATION
adjudicationPoints.body: Same mechanism as AP-01-TAILEDGEDROP, on a different species. BEHENTRIMONIUM METHOSULFATE is declared at rank 9 and PARFUM at rank 10, so the second cationic is a tail_index − 1 species; removing it per §9.1's tail-edge exclusion leaves CETRIMONIUM CHLORIDE @6 as the only cationic and S1 fails. With S1 mandatory, `conditioning_level` drops from `high` to `moderate`. The ledger's R3 line predicts two such drops (#06, #12) and five surviving `high` calls; applying the standard as written gives four drops (#01, #03, #06, #12) and three surviving (#04, #05, #10). The divergence is flagged, not forced. It is also sharply visible in the twin pair: #10 Bali Curls Deep Repair carries the SAME two cationics at ranks 8 and 10 against a marker at 12, so both survive the exclusion and it keeps `high`. Two near-identical formulas from one brand now differ on field 1 because of a two-rank difference in where a preservative was printed. That is either the boundary band doing its job or the band being too wide; §9.1 records the width as the open calibration question, and this pair is the cohort's cleanest test of it.
